label: 1 UNS explorer
info:
Subscribes to all **events** of the line in the Unified Namespace (UNS) and counts them per
event type.

- Topic scheme: `vf/plant01/final-assembly/line01/{device}/event/{event}` (see docs/interfaces/uns.md)
- `+` matches exactly one topic level (the device), `#` everything below `event/`
- Payload: flat JSON object with `event`, `device`, `session`, `seq`, `ts` and event specific fields

Start the factory (Godot) and open the debug sidebar (bug icon, top right).

Ideas: also count per device; subscribe to telemetry `vf/plant01/final-assembly/line01/plc01/#` instead (much more traffic!).

name: UNS explorer: count line events per type (double click for details)
info: Every event of every device arrives at the mqtt-in node, the function keeps a counter per event type in its node context and sends the whole table on. `seq` is a per-session event counter, so a gap means that events were lost (e.g. during a reconnect).

name: count per event type

label: 2 Reject alarm
info:
Raises an alarm when too many parts fail the colour inspection.

1. `part_inspected` events of PLC01 arrive (field `result`: 1 = OK, 2 = reject)
2. the switch node lets only rejects pass
3. the function keeps the reject times of the last `WINDOW_S` seconds (sliding window) and emits an alert
   when there are more than `LIMIT` of them (at most one alert per window)
4. the change node sets the alert topic, the mqtt-out node publishes it to `vf/plant01/final-assembly/line01/sandbox/alert`

Watch the alert e.g. with MQTT Explorer or `mosquitto_sub -h localhost -t 'vf/plant01/final-assembly/line01/sandbox/#' -v`.
The "simulated reject" inject node feeds a fake event directly into the switch (it is **not** published to the
broker, so the MES does not see it) - click it a few times to test without the factory.

name: Reject alarm: > LIMIT rejects within WINDOW_S seconds -> alert topic
info: Window length and limit are constants at the top of the function node. Time base is the event timestamp `ts` (simulation time), so the alarm also works in faster-than-real-time runs.

name: sliding window

label: 3 Read the AAS
info:
Reads the live counters of the PLC from its digital twin (AAS) via the AAS REST API.

- Submodel id: `https://virtual-factory.example/ids/sm/PLC01/OperationalData/1`
- In URLs, ids are **base64url** encoded (RFC 4648, `-` and `_` instead of `+` and `/`, no `=` padding)
- `GET http://aas-env:8091/submodels/{base64url id}/$value` returns the values only (ValueOnly format, numbers as strings)
- `aas-env` is the compose service name; from the host use `http://localhost:8091` (Swagger UI: `/swagger`)

The counters are written into the AAS by the bridge service from the UNS telemetry (counters are discrete: written on change).
Ideas: add a repeat interval to the inject node; read another submodel (e.g. LINE01 EnergyConsumption).

name: Read the AAS: PLC01 OperationalData -> part counters
info: Click the button of the inject node. The result appears in the debug sidebar and as node status.

name: build URL (base64url id)

label: 4 Call an AAS operation
info:
Commands the line through its digital twin: invokes the operation
`ExecutePackMLCommand` of the LINE01 submodel `LineControl`.

- `POST http://aas-env:8091/submodels/{base64url id}/submodel-elements/ExecutePackMLCommand/invoke`
- Body: `inputArguments` (OperationVariables, here the Property `Command`) + `clientTimeoutDuration`
- BaSyx delegates the call to the ops-gateway, which sends the PackML command to the PLC over the UNS and waits for
  the resulting state. Output arguments: `Accepted`, `State`, `Message`.
- Commands: Start, Stop, Hold, Unhold, Reset, Suspend, Unsuspend, Abort, Clear. Commands not allowed in the
  current PackML state are rejected (`Accepted` = false, reason in `Message`).

**This really commands the running line.** Hold pauses it, Unhold continues.

name: Call an AAS operation: LINE01 LineControl/ExecutePackMLCommand
info: Duplicate an inject node and change its payload to try other commands (e.g. Stop, Reset, Start).
